title: My management game’s HUD was a mess. We drew five other options. Which would you ship?
author: Don_InterestingSys
selftext:
I'm making Under Management, a 3D dungeon-management game: you dig out a house, hire staff, and defend the gold from adventurers. There are no unit orders, so during a raid you need to \*watch the action\*

And the screen was fighting you: 398 words of panels, logs and widgets.

So we mocked five replacements over the same screenshot, each played through calm → raid → pause → a "show everything" key:

Out of 50 iterations these stood out as the best

\- A · Figures on the house. Every number sits on the thing it measures (gold on the hoard, heat on the fire, the raid countdown on its road). One small page of notes. 82 words calm / 45 in a raid.

\- B · One rule, one line. Four fixed figures in a corner, one note at a time. 54 / 27.

\- C · One open page. Everything on one sheet that turns when the bell rings. 85 / 49.

\- D · Whatever he's holding. The deputy's pen, watch, ledger or lamp decides what's shown. 87 / 60.

\- E · Tags tied to things. Paper dockets tied to rooms and staff, nothing at the screen's edges. 74 / 37.

I know which way I'm leaning... but I liked the old interface every step along the way that it went from simple to cluttered mess until one day a play tester said it was a mess, so, yeah, I could use help

(The numbers and names in the mocks are placeholders. The tool menu is trimmed in all five, so the real word counts will be a bit higher. The mocks were drawn with Claude Fable 5.2 from a shared brief and ate half of my weekly subscription; happy to share the prompts.  The build will go via Opus 5.5)

comments.author: Don_InterestingSys
comments.body: oh, and if you want to play test I could use your help

comments.author: Itchy_Ship2584
comments.body:
B is the only one i'd take

might be because all the claude-text is just instantly oof and B is the only one that isn't screaming it, although it still has that yellow line which inot great

replies.author: Don_InterestingSys
replies.body: do you mean the yellow line on the bottom menu?  any suggestions on how you'd fix that?

replies.author: Don_InterestingSys
replies.body: or do you mean the test at the top?

comments.author: StoneCypher
comments.body:
i would say you’re asking us to pick between claude’s ideas for you, and none of these are good 

you’re deferring too much of the design.  this will yield bad product.  go back to making your own choices

replies.author: Don_InterestingSys
replies.body:
that's not really my intent.  I'm looking for preferences from people here, I already have the AI's preference and I don't agree with it.  

I'm ultimately the one who will decide which of these to use if any, or if I pull from a few or go back to tweaking the old interface.  After that choice I'll show it to some more people and listen to what they say and consider it as well.  I started examining other choices because of feedback from a play tester and while one option is just to clean up the existing interface a little I thought that trying on a few complete redesigns might be interesting.

I took inspiration from a game who's interface I like but wasn't sure how it would fit in my game.  Claude let me try some iterations so I can see it 'in game'.  What I see that I dislike the most is the half-and-half mixes that keep a bit of the old interface and combine it with the new one.

any specific reason you dislike one of them?  anything you'd keep?

replies.author: StoneCypher
replies.body:
you know how everyone hates claude written comments?  if they’re raw they can complain about the em dashes and the it’s not x it’s y, but even after a human tries to fix it, there’s that characteristic meter, the unnecessary explanations and callouts, the paragraphs that just don’t need to be there?

that’s what this graphic design looks like 

maybe you’re going to take away the super headers, remove the gross fonts, make it not beige

fundamentally though, claude is a machine that takes the average of everything it’s seen and predicts that

no amount of retooling will make that not theseus’ ship from the catalogue 

games need distinct character

fixing it is more work than doing it from scratch and it can’t be entirely fixed

throwing it out is the only move that will lead to quality 

the more you study this, the less you will be able to get away from the mediocrity machine’s design

replies.author: Don_InterestingSys
replies.body: thanks for taking the time to give me a useful comment.  I do appreciate that
